newsitem.title: UK: Brady bonds see sluggish pre-weekend trade-dealers.
newsitem.headline: Brady bonds see sluggish pre-weekend trade-dealers.

text.p: The Brady market saw little change from overnight prices in sluggish pre-weekend trade, dealers said on Friday.

"Its dead quiet, there's nothing to say, prices are more or less unchanged...everyone is waiting for the U.S. data due next week. The Brady market is still very much governed by the U.S. bond market which is under a bit of pressure," a dealer said.
He said there was a brief flurry of activity in Russia which "was all over in about three seconds".
Russian VN US$ was up 1/2, bid at 78-3/8 at 1145 GMT.

Analysts said next week's busy calendar of significant economic data, remarks by Federal Reserve governor Laurence Meyer and the substantial new supply auctioned this week combined to pressure prices of U.S. government securities.

The benchmark 30-year Treasury yielded 7.138 percent at 1130 GMT. "Our outlook (for the Brady market) is negative for the next six to eight months. Any up-trade that we have had has been an opportunity to sell as far as we are concerned," another dealer said.
"When Treasuries break out of the range they will really break out and then we'll see some action in the Brady market," he added.
